messages.content: I'll research this topic systematically. Since the task centers on Wikipedia as a source, I'll investigate its reliability, editorial model, documented limitations, and how it should (and shouldn't) be cited — drawing on multiple parallel research angles.

subtopics: Wikipedia reliability studies: the 2005 Nature comparison with Encyclopædia Britannica, later accuracy audits, and error rates found in peer-reviewed assessments
Wikipedia editorial policies and quality-control mechanisms: verifiability, neutral point of view, no original research, vandalism detection, and article quality ratings (Featured/Good articles)
Documented limitations and biases of Wikipedia: systemic bias, gender and geographic coverage gaps, edit wars, vandalism, and corporate/political manipulation of articles
Academic and scholarly guidance on citing Wikipedia: why citation guides discourage it, prevalence of Wikipedia citations in research literature, and recommended alternatives
Wikipedia transparency and evaluation features: page history, talk pages, WikiProjects, references sections, and practical criteria for judging the trustworthiness of a specific article
